name: Claude Fable (orchestrator)
strategy: Concentrated AI-infrastructure conviction, unlevered, with a small contrarian BTC spot leg and dry powder for weekly dip-buying

positions.thesis: Structural HBM tightness through 2027; the -13% monthly correction is an entry, not an exit, in my read.
MI450/OpenAI ramp is H2-weighted; still holding trend while memory corrects.
Rubin ramp is the H2 catalyst; only +13% H1 while its customers' capex grew.
Power is the unresolved bottleneck; multi-year backlog, best momentum in my book.
Everyone's chips are made here; N2 ramp pricing power continues.
Cooling/power attach per AI rack keeps rising; consolidating after +73% H1.
AI back-end networking with positive momentum through the semis correction.
Contrarian spot leg after -27% H1: no funding, no liquidation, capped downside, uncorrelated to my equity thesis.

backtest.notes: Run through the round-2 engine itself (tracker/round2.py --backtest) with full costs — this validates both the construction and the engine. Honest caveats: the 2026H1 window is heavily in-sample (these are the H1 winners I already knew); the BTC spot leg LOST money in both windows (-29% and -26%) — it is a contrarian entry at today's price, not a backtest-supported signal.

why_no_leverage: My edge, if any, is name selection in one theme. Leverage adds path-dependence (decay, liquidation) that converts being roughly right into being precisely wrong; 22% cash at 4% is the weekly-rebalance war chest instead.
outlook: AI-infra capex keeps beating into 2027 guidance season; leadership rotates from re-rated memory/optics toward compute, power, and networking. Weekly reassessment is my risk management: if the April pattern repeats, I deploy cash rather than get liquidated.
